subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Oil and Gas Pipelines: Moving Energy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Oil and Gas Pipelines: Moving Energy.

hook.text: Pipelines carry oil and gas thousands of miles across continents.

buildup.text: Booster stations add pressure every 50-100 miles to keep flow going.

discovery.text: Pig devices travel inside the pipe to clean walls and inspect for cracks.

twist.text: A pinhole leak underground can go undetected for weeks, spilling thousands of barrels.

climax.text: Modern pipelines use fiber-optic sensors to detect leaks in real time.

punchline.text: Moving fuel by pipe is cheap — if you keep it sealed.

quiz.question: What are pipeline 'pigs' used for?
options: Pumping stations that boost pressure along the route
Devices that travel inside the pipe to clean it and inspect for damage
Valves that shut off flow in an emergency
